mainTopic: What a נזיר's טומאה after one offering undoes, and who should become טמא for a מת מצוה: a כהן גדול or a נזיר
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about a נזיר who becomes טמא after the blood of one of his end-of-term offerings has already been sprinkled. רבי אליעזר says the טומאה is סותר everything. The חכמים say he brings the rest of his offerings, and they back this up with the story of מרים התרמודית. The גמרא asks how this fits with רבי אליעזר's own rule elsewhere, that טומאה after the term undoes only seven days. רב answers that 'everything' here means all the offerings, not the days of נזירות. The wording of the חכמים and the story of מרים both support רב's answer. After the הדרן for פרק שלשה מינין, a new משנה teaches that a כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become טמא even for relatives, but must become טמא for a מת מצוה. If both of them find one together, רבי אליעזר says the כהן גדול should become טמא, because a נזיר would have to bring a קרבן. The חכמים say the נזיר should become טמא, because a כהן's holiness is permanent. The גמרא then starts comparing other kinds of people, beginning with a כהן גדול anointed with שמן המשחה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case and the dispute: a נזיר becomes impure after one offering
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר had the blood of one offering sprinkled for him and then became טמא. רבי אליעזר says it is סותר everything. חכמים say he brings the rest of his offerings and becomes pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone had the blood of one of his offerings sprinkled for him, and then he became impure. רבי אליעזר says: it undoes everything. The חכמים say: he should bring the rest of his offerings and become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a case and a disagreement. A נזיר is in the middle of bringing his end-of-term offerings and becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of his term, a נזיר brings three offerings. Here the blood of one was already sprinkled when he became טמא. רבי אליעזר says the טומאה undoes 'everything,' but he does not say what 'everything' means. חכמים say the offerings already brought still count, so he only needs to finish the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
Was sprinkled (the blood of an offering on the מזבח)
The bloods, meaning the blood of the offerings
Undoes or cancels, used for something that wipes out what was already counted or done
And he became ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: 'סותר את הכל' sounds like he must restart his whole נזירות. Hold off on deciding that. The גמרא is about to ask exactly what 'everything' means.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One on whose behalf there was sprinkled
the blood of one of the offerings, and then he became impure,
phrases.notes: He means one of the three offerings a נזיר brings when his term ends.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it undoes everything.
And the Rabbis say:
Let him bring the rest of his offerings and be purified.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים וְנִטְמָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the טומאה is סותר everything. חכמים: he brings his remaining offerings and becomes pure.

steps.title: The story of מרים התרמודית supports the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: חכמים bring a real case. מרים התרמודית became טמא after one of her offerings was sprinkled, and the חכמים ruled she should bring the rest of her offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There was a case with מרים התרמודית. The blood of one of her offerings was sprinkled for her. People came and told her that her daughter was dangerously ill. She went and found that her daughter had died. The חכמים said: she should bring the rest of her offerings and become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים back up their view with a story where their ruling was actually applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים became טמא מת when she found her daughter dead. This happened after one of her offerings had already been brought, which is exactly the case of the משנה. The ruling was that the offering already brought still counts, so she only completes the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A real incident brought as a precedent
From the place called תרמוד
Dangerously ill, close to death

phrases.english: They said to him: There was an incident with Miriam of Tarmod,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אליעזר. The חכמים are answering him.

phrases.english: for whom the blood of one of the offerings was sprinkled,
and people came and told her about her daughter
that she was dangerously ill,
and she went and found that she had died.
phrases.notes: Being there with her dead daughter made her טמאת מת.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said:
Let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified.

steps.raayaObject: The view of חכמים that he brings the rest of his offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The actual ruling given for מרים התרמודית

steps.title: Contradiction: elsewhere רבי אליעזר says only seven days are undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר can say 'everything' is undone, when elsewhere he says טומאה after the term undoes only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה teaches that רבי אליעזר says it undoes everything. But didn't רבי אליעזר say: any טומאה after the term is complete undoes seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two statements of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מסכת, רבי אליעזר ruled that a נזיר who becomes טמא after finishing his term loses only seven days. Our נזיר has also finished his term. So why would רבי אליעזר now say the טומאה undoes 'everything'?

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא
It teaches, used when quoting the משנה
But didn't he say? This introduces a contradicting statement.
The completion (of the term of נזירות)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches: Rabbi Eliezer says:
it undoes everything.
But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
Any impurity after the completion of the term undoes seven days!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's words 'סותר את הכל' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds elsewhere that טומאה after the term undoes only seven days, so 'everything' contradicts his own view.

steps.title: רב: 'everything' means all his offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'סותר' in our משנה refers to the offerings. Even the offering already brought must be brought again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: What does 'undoes' mean when רבי אליעזר says it? It undoes his offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב solves the contradiction by explaining what 'everything' means in רבי אליעזר's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings are about different things. The seven-day rule tells us how many days of נזירות are lost. Our משנה tells us that the offering already sprinkled no longer counts, so all the קרבנות must be brought again.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What does it mean?
That he says
His offerings

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue only about the offerings: all of them again, or only the rest.

phrases.english: Rav said:
What is the 'undoes'
that Rabbi Eliezer says here?
It undoes his offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַאי סוֹתֵר נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word: 'everything' refers to the offerings, not the days of נזירות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'סותר את הכל' means the whole term of נזירות is lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'סותר' means all his קרבנות must be brought again. The seven-day rule still stands.

steps.title: Support from how the חכמים word their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב's reading makes sense, since the חכמים answer by saying 'bring the rest of the offerings.' That shows the argument is about offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also reasonable to say this, since the משנה teaches: 'And the חכמים say: let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב's explanation from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים answer רבי אליעזר by talking only about 'the rest of the offerings.' If רבי אליעזר meant the whole term is lost, that would be a strange reply. So the two sides must be arguing about the offerings, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable, used to bring support for what was just said
Since it teaches
Learn from it, meaning the proof works

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since it teaches: And the Rabbis say:
Let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified,
phrases.notes: The point is the words 'rest of the offerings.' That shows the argument is about offerings.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.raayaObject: רב's reading that the מחלוקת is about the offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of חכמים in the משנה: 'bring the rest of her offerings'

steps.title: The story of מרים also shows the argument is about offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the story of מרים התרמודית again. The ruling there was about her remaining offerings, which confirms רב's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also the incident with מרים התרמודית: the blood of one of her offerings was sprinkled for her, and people came and told her that her daughter was dangerously ill. She went and found that she had died, and the חכמים said: she should bring the rest of her offerings and become pure. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support for רב from the story at the end of the משנה, and then concludes that רב is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים told רבי אליעזר this story as an answer to him. Its ruling is only about her remaining offerings, so the disagreement must also be about offerings. The גמרא repeats the story here for this new purpose and closes with 'שמע מינה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Also
And they informed her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's 'סותר את הכל' means all the קרבנות must be brought again, not that the whole נזירות restarts. Both the wording of חכמים and the story of מרים support this.

phrases.english: And also the incident with Miriam of Tarmod,
for whom the blood of one of the offerings was sprinkled,
and people came and informed her about her daughter
that she was dangerously ill,
and she went and found that she had died,
and the Rabbis said:
Let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified.
Learn from this.

steps.raayaObject: רב's reading that the מחלוקת is about the offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of מרים התרמודית in the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב is right: רבי אליעזר's 'everything' refers to the offerings.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק שלשה מינין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the פרק called שלשה מינין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'Three Kinds.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the previous פרק. It is not part of any argument. It just marks that the פרק has ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פרק is named after its opening words. This one began with the three kinds of things forbidden to a נזיר. The הדרן is a way of saying goodbye and promising to come back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said at the end of a פרק.
Three kinds. This is the name of the פרק that just ended, after the three things forbidden to a נזיר.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Three Kinds'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the entire פרק whose final discussion was רב's explanation of the dispute about the offerings (steps 4-6).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of שלשה מינין is finished. A new פרק begins.

steps.title: A כהן גדול and a נזיר may become טמא only for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens. A כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become טמא even for their relatives, but they do become טמא for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become טמא for their relatives, but they may become טמא for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a basic rule. A כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become טמא even for close family, but they must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן is allowed to become טמא for close relatives. A כהן גדול and a נזיר are not allowed, even for them. But a מת מצוה is a body with no one else to bury it, and caring for it overrides even their strict rules.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
A person who took a vow of נזירות
Become ritually impure (טמא)
A dead body with no one else to bury it. Whoever finds it must bury it.

steps.whatToRemember: Even the strictest people, a כהן גדול and a נזיר, must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: A High Priest and a nazir
do not become impure for their relatives,
but they do become impure for a met מצוה.
phrases.notes: A מת מצוה is a body with no one else around to bury it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְנָזִיר אֵין מִיטַּמְּאִין לִקְרוֹבֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become טמא for relatives, but they must become טמא for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: Both find a מת מצוה: who should become טמא?
steps.stepSummary: If a כהן גדול and a נזיר find a מת מצוה together, רבי אליעזר says the כהן גדול should become טמא. The חכמים say the נזיר should, and not even a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were walking on the road and found a מת מצוה, רבי אליעזר says the כהן גדול should become טמא and not the נזיר. The חכמים say the נזיר should become טמא, and not even a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a case where both people find the body together, and only one needs to become טמא. רבי אליעזר and the חכמים disagree about which one it should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר wants to protect the נזיר. The חכמים want to protect the כהן. The חכמים go further: even a regular כהן should stay טהור rather than the נזיר, so a כהן גדול certainly should.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking along the road
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
Let him become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the body must be buried. The only question is which of the two people should do it.

phrases.english: If they were walking along the road
and they found a met מצוה —
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: יִטַּמֵּא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְאַל יִטַּמֵּא נָזִיר.
phrases.english: Let the High Priest become impure, and let the nazir not become impure.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: יִטַּמֵּא נָזִיר, וְאַל יִטַּמֵּא כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: Let the nazir become impure, and let not even a regular priest become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ וּמָצְאוּ מֵת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 8 to a case where both people are present together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר says the כהן גדול becomes טמא. The חכמים say the נזיר does, and not even a regular כהן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason: the נזיר would need a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that the כהן should become טמא because he brings no קרבן for it, while a נזיר does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: Let the כהן become טמא, since he does not bring a קרבן for his טומאה. Let the נזיר not become טמא, since he does bring a קרבן for his טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the reason for his view. A נזיר who becomes טמא has to bring a קרבן, but a כהן does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר measures how serious the טומאה is by what it costs afterward. For a נזיר, טומאה brings a required קרבן and more. For a כהן, it has no such cost, so it is the lighter loss.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering
His impurity

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
Let the priest become impure —
since he does not bring an offering for his impurity,
and let the nazir not become impure —
since he brings an offering for his impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the כהן גדול should become טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical argument: a נזיר's טומאה requires a קרבן, and a כהן's does not.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: a כהן's holiness is permanent
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond that the נזיר should become טמא, because his holiness is temporary, while a כהן's holiness lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Let the נזיר become טמא, since his holiness is not permanent. Let the כהן not become טמא, since his holiness is permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי אליעזר with a different way to measure. They look at how lasting each person's holiness is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not deny that the נזיר brings a קרבן. They argue that this matters less. A נזיר's holiness lasts only for the time of his vow, but a כהן is holy for his whole life, so his holiness deserves more protection.

keyTerms.meaning: His holiness
Permanent holiness that lasts forever

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר asks which טומאה costs more, the one that requires a קרבן. The חכמים ask whose holiness is more lasting, the כהן's permanent holiness.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Let the nazir become impure —
since his holiness is not a permanent holiness,
and let the priest not become impure —
since his holiness is a permanent holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ יִטַּמֵּא נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי אליעזר's reasoning from step 10 with a competing reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's conclusion, not the fact that a נזיר brings a קרבן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר looks only at the cost of the טומאה and ignores that a כהן's holiness is permanent.

steps.title: The גמרא grants that the dispute about a כהן גדול and a נזיר is clear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with בשלמא: in the case of a כהן גדול and a נזיר, it is clear that each side thinks a different one is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, with a כהן גדול and a נזיר, this one holds the כהן גדול is more important, and that one holds the נזיר is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It first says that the case of a כהן גדול versus a נזיר makes sense, so it can then ask about other pairs of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בשלמא means 'it makes sense here.' It signals that a 'but what about' question is coming next. The גמרא explains the משנה's dispute simply: the חכמים think the כהן גדול is more important to keep טהור, and רבי אליעזר thinks the נזיר is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Granted, this case makes sense. It signals that a question about another case is coming.
Is more important, here meaning the one who should be kept טהור

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. The first 'this one' (כהן גדול is more important) is the חכמים. The second (נזיר is more important) is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Gemara: Granted, a High Priest and a nazir,
this one holds: the High Priest is more important,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים. They want to keep the כהן גדול טהור.

phrases.english: and this one holds: the nazir is more important.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר. He wants to keep the נזיר טהור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first step on the משנה. It sums up the dispute of steps 9-11 to prepare a question about other kinds of people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setting up a question: the כהן גדול and נזיר case is clear, but how does this dispute apply to other pairs of people, such as different kinds of כהן גדול?

steps.title: Naming the כהן גדול anointed with the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names a specific type of כהן גדול, one who was anointed with שמן המשחה. This sets up a comparison or question that continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: One anointed with the anointing oil...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is naming a specific kind of כהן גדול, the one anointed with שמן המשחה. This is a setup line that prepares the next question, which continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the case was a general כהן גדול facing a נזיר. Here the גמרא points to one particular kind of כהן גדול, the one who became כהן גדול by being anointed with the special oil. The full question about him comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Anointed. A כהן גדול who was put into office by having the special oil poured on him.
The anointing oil, the special holy oil used to anoint the כהן גדול.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full statement by itself. It only names the person the גמרא is about to discuss, so keep reading to get the actual question.

phrases.english: One anointed with the anointing oil
phrases.notes: That's a כהן גדול who was put into office by being anointed with the special holy oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 12 opened with בשלמא, saying the כהן גדול and נזיר case makes sense as a מחלוקת. This line starts naming the next case the גמרא wants to look at: a specific type of כהן גדול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question is still being set up. This line names its subject: the כהן גדול anointed with שמן המשחה.
